You wrote off the whole laptop. Two years later, you sell it for seven hundred. Here's the catch.
line01
Last time: a two-thousand-dollar laptop, claimed one hundred percent. Its tax value is now zero.
line02
Sell it for seven hundred, and that zero goes negative: minus seven hundred.
line03
CRA calls that recapture. It goes straight back into your business income.
line04
For our Manitoba freelancer, that's about two hundred and fifty dollars in tax and CPP.
line05
Fair, really. You deducted value the laptop never actually lost.
line06
The fix: buy the replacement in the same year. Its cost goes into the class first.
line07
Twenty-five hundred new, minus seven hundred sold: eighteen hundred left to claim. No recapture.
line08
But what if the laptop is only sixty percent for work?
line09
Reply sixty, and we'll run it.
